## Summary

I implemented the complete webshop application described in the Projektauftrag, end to end:

**Backend** (ASP.NET Core 10 / EF Core 10 / SQL Server) — `seed-b-backend.Api`:
- Domain model: `Category` (self-referencing for the 2-level hierarchy, with per-subcategory `PropertyNames`), `Product` (with JSON-backed `Properties` dictionary), `Supplier`, `ProductOffer`, `Review`, `Order`/`OrderItem`.
- `CategoriesController`, `ProductsController` (paginated/sortable/filterable/searchable list, detail view with view-counter increment, review upsert), `OrdersController` (atomic order creation that rejects the whole order on an empty cart, invalid quantity, or a no-longer-available offer — B-F14 — and freezes supplier/price per line at order time — B-F10).
- `DataSeeder` loads `anfangsdatenbestand.json` on first startup only, via `dotnet ef` migrations applied automatically (`Database.Migrate()`).
- No cart persistence server-side by design: since there's no login and checkout happens in one sitting, the cart lives entirely in the Angular client and is only sent to the server at order time.
- 17 xUnit tests (EF Core InMemory) covering listing/filtering/sorting, view-count increments, review upsert, and all order-validation branches — all passing.

**Frontend** (Angular 22, standalone components, signals) — `seed-b-frontend`:
- Routes: product list, product detail, cart, checkout, order confirmation.
- `CartService` (signal-based, localStorage-persisted, merges same product+supplier lines, keeps different suppliers separate per B-F8).
- Category nav, search, sort, dynamic category-specific property filters, pagination; product detail with supplier/price selection, review form; checkout with delivery/contact form and server-side validation error display.
- 13 Vitest tests (cart logic, HTTP query building) — all passing.

**Verified live** against a real SQL Server instance and a running `ng serve` + proxy: browsed, filtered, sorted, viewed a product (counter incremented), submitted a review (average updated live), added to cart, checked out, and confirmed the order — with the cart clearing afterward and no console errors, screenshots inspected at each step.

Both backend and frontend build cleanly. I stopped the dev processes and dropped the test database afterward so the app will reseed cleanly on next start.
